paper text.text: The nonplanar graph $H$ has no $K_5$ minor, so it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. If $bd$ is present, Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion} applied to the toroidal graph $G-bd$ makes $H-bd$ planar, so every such subdivision uses $bd$. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with the five attachments and the fixed planar graph on them consisting of $ab,ac,ad,ae$, together with $bd$ when present. The reduction preserves the connected interior, all five attachments and the nonplanarity of the completion, so the resulting minor is nontoroidal by Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion}. Minimality forces the reduction to be trivial. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives $217{,}376$ candidates. All except $\mathfrak T_{20},\mathfrak T_{23}$ have a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, a proper nontoroidal minor, or two twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices~\supp{E22}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...

disjoint twin triples.meaning: Section 6 assumes any two twin triples share exactly one vertex
